messages:
Nina: FYI the release cut is blocked, preflight-windows job failed after restoring cache. Tests hit lots of IO errors and then the smoke suite errored on long path names.
Arjun: Can you paste the failing stack?
Nina: snippet from the runner:
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File \"/runner/_work/redwood/redwood/tests/smoke_windows.py\", line 42, in setUp
    open('\\?\\C:\\actions\\_work\\redwood\\artifacts\\very_long_unpacked_path\\payload.bin', 'rb')
OSError: [Errno 36] File name too long
```
Ken: Interesting: the artifact cache step reported an 401 in the same job earlier: `artifact-restore: GET https://storage.internal/... 401 Unauthorized`. The runner then unpacks a partial archive which created a nested temp dir.
ops-bot: CI: job 4648 (preflight-windows) failed during artifact-restore with 401. Full logs: https://ci.internal/4648 :warning:
Marta (PM): If we pause the cut here please say so, I'll update release communications. Any quick unblock?
Arjun: Two likely culprits: (A) token rotation changed the signer so presigned URLs are invalid; (B) cache-prune process removed the object causing auth to fail. I'll check signer logs.
Nina: Reproducer: I downloaded the artifact URL from the job and it works for ~90s then returns 401. Might be short expiry or clock skew.
Ken: We recently merged the staging-credentials rotation that reduced presign expiry to 60s for security. That was supposed to be paired with a runner change to download immediately, but the runner queue delays >2m in peak.
Arjun: Quick mitigations ranked: 1) Increase presign expiry to 900s (fast config change in publisher); 2) Re-run job on less busy runners (manual queue routing); 3) Revert the staging-credentials rotation (higher blast radius).
Marta (PM): Prefer config change over revert. Do we have an estimate for the presign tweak?
Arjun: I can open a one-line change in staging-publish to bump expiry. Test + deploy should be ~20m.
Nina: Can we also add a guard in the runner to validate the artifact before unpacking to avoid partial unpack creating super-long paths? That would prevent the Windows path error from cascading.
Ken: I'll prototype a small change: unpack into short fixed dir %RUNNER_TEMP%\\cache_unpack and validate tarball checksum before extraction. Low-risk.
deploy-bot: deploybot: Manual hold applied to release/cut/2025-03-05 by Nina  promotion blocked.
Marta (PM): Please keep the hold until preflight-green. I'll notify stakeholders.
Arjun: Opening PR to increase presign TTL now (staging-publisher: presign_expires=900). Will request a quick deployment.
Nina: I'll patch the windows runner job to use the short unpack dir and add a checksum sanity check; pushing as a separate small PR so CI can run in parallel.
Ken: If presign patch lands fast we can requeue preflight immediately. If not, runner patch is a fallback and then we can consider reverting staging-credentials only if both fail.
ops-bot: CI: presign-ttl PR deployment queued by Arjun.
Arjun: Update: presign TTL PR merged and deployed to staging. Generated presigned URL now valid for 15m in test.
Nina: Rerunning preflight on a fresh runner now: job 4650 queued.
ops-bot: CI: preflight-windows #4650 started.
Ken: If we still see 401s after this, we should check clock sync on runners - drift would make presigned URLs appear expired.
Nina: Preflight 4650 passed artifact restore and unpack cleanly. Smoke tests still running.
ops-bot: CI: preflight-windows #4650 finished: SUCCESS :tada:
deploy-bot: deploybot: Manual hold removed on release/cut/2025-03-05 by Nina  promotion allowed.
Marta (PM): Thanks team. I'll update release notes: note about delayed cut cleared, root cause was presign expiry + unpack path edge for windows.
Nina: Postmortem action items: 1) revert presign TTL reduction if it reappears, 2) keep runner unpack dir short on windows, 3) add presign TTL safety margin in publisher. I'll open a follow-up doc.
Arjun: Adding a small CI test that attempts to download presigned URLs with simulated queue delay to catch this earlier.
Marta (PM): Closing loop  mark this cut as moved forward and include the postmortem link in release notes later.
